response: Yes, prostate specific antigen (PSA) levels may need to be adjusted for body mass index (BMI) because studies have shown that PSA levels can be lower in men with higher BMI. This is thought to be due to the dilutional effect of a larger blood volume in men with higher BMI, which can lead to lower PSA concentrations. Adjusting PSA levels for BMI may help improve the accuracy of PSA testing for prostate cancer detection.
